subject: Action: Make-good & rate-limit roadmap for Kestrel Systems — exec review
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Grady <tgrady@kestrel.ai>, contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rates & timeouts this morning — immediate action required

Jordan —

We had a major degradation on our integration this morning between 06:45 and 09:15 UTC (roughly 2.5 hours) where ~18% of inference requests returned 5xx/429 or timed out. This caused retries from our side which amplified the problem and impacted customer-facing latency. We've attached a sample of our request logs and invoices for impacted periods.

Elena Ruiz
VP Engineering, Kestrel Systems
elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai

---
Attachment: kestrel-usage-sample.csv (3.2MB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rates & timeouts this morning — immediate action required

Elena — thank you for the callout and the logs. I’m escalating to ops now (cc'd). We see correlated anomalies in our edge telemetry (spike in queued requests then 429 throttles). Primary asks from our side while we investigate:

- Can you confirm if you applied any client-side retry policy during the window?
- Any traffic pattern changes (burst from a job) we should know about?

We’ll take ownership of a thorough postmortem and propose a make-good. I’ll have an initial ops remediation + proposed credit schedule in the afternoon.

-Jordan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rates & timeouts this morning — immediate action required

Quick summary from ops after triage:
- Root cause: a mis-specified autoscale policy on the dedicated pool serving Kestrel which left steady-state concurrency low during a sudden burst (internal ref OPS-7321).
- Secondary impact: our global rate limiter then produced 429s once queue depth exceeded soft thresholds.
- Timeline: anomaly detected 06:40 UTC, initial mitigation (temporary pool increase + relaxed rate limit) at 07:05 UTC, full stabilization at 09:30 UTC.

Proposed immediate remediation steps:
1) Disable the problematic autoscale rule and apply conservative concurrency floor for Kestrel (done as of 10:00 PDT).
2) Add a targeted rate-limit exception window and backoff-smoothing for retries.
3) Postmortem with timeline + commit to a config guardrail.

I’ll attach the incident report draft and the raw graphs.

-Hannah
Head of Reliability — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: incident-report-20260909.pdf (1.1MB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed make-good and short-term SL adjustments for Kestrel (draft)

Elena / Jordan / team —

Thank you for patience. Based on the impact window and Kestrel's billing, the initial offer we propose is:

1) Usage credit equal to 35% of daily billed inference units for the impacted day (applied as account credit).
2) One month of elevated SLA monitoring (no-cost) with 2x retention for traces relevant to your endpoints.
3) Ops commitment: configured guardrail + runbook and a joint run-through with your engineering team this week.

We believe this is fair given the root cause profile; happy to escalate to leadership for adjustments if the credit is insufficient. Please advise if legal/POC need a formal agreement or a signed make-good letter.

-Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: proposed-makegood-offer-20260909.pdf (42KB)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Grady <tgrady@kestrel.ai>, contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed make-good and short-term SL adjustments for Kestrel (draft)

Rishi — thanks for the quick proposal. Kestrel appreciates the proactive ops commitments. On credits: our finance team requests a formal credit calculation showing the dollar value equivalent (we pay monthly invoice X; please show how 35% maps to an ACV adjustment). Also: because retries caused customer-visible latency, we require a one-time service credit equal to 50% of the impacted day's bill OR a guaranteed runway of 2 months of credits capped at the same value — whichever is larger. Please escalate if you can’t approve that.

We’ll pause escalation to legal while you provide the dollar calculation.

—Elena
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed make-good and short-term SL adjustments for Kestrel (draft)

Elena / Kestrel team —

I’m Jordan’s director and looped in because Kestrel is a strategic account. We’ve computed the dollar mapping for the 35% usage credit: based on your July invoice and posted rates, the 35% credit equals $38,750 for the impacted day. We can instead offer the alternate settlement you requested: either a one-time 50% credit ($55,350) or a two-month credit run-rate capped at that amount (structured over future invoices).

Our recommended settlement (to close quickly while we implement guardrails):
- Immediate one-time credit of 40% ($44,280) applied to your next invoice.
- Joint ops run-through this week and a waived professional-services session to review integration best practices.
- SLA amendment: we’ll add an explicit retry-throttle mitigation clause and a 30-day extended monitoring window.

If that’s acceptable I’ll sign the make-good letter and route to contracts.

-Sergio
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Tom Grady <tgrady@kestrel.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrel.ai>, contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed make-good and short-term SL adjustments for Kestrel (draft)

Sergio — thanks. Kestrel will accept the 40% one-time credit and the run-through. Please send the make-good letter and confirmation of dates for the ops session (we prefer Fri 2026-09-17 or Mon 2026-09-20). Contracts will sign on receipt of the finalized letter and allocation to our account.

-Tom
Director, Procurement — Kestrel Systems
